correctness.rationale: Every selected rook cell is an edge of \(K_{m,n}\); maximum induced degree one forces and is forced by vertex-disjoint components \(K_{1,1}\), \(K_{1,2}\), or \(K_{2,1}\). With component counts \(a,b,c\), the used row/column counts are \(r=a+b+2c\) and \(s=a+2b+c\). An exhaustive one-cell-addition analysis proves maximality if and only if both sides are fully used or no isolated component exists and at least one side is fully used. Labeled slot partitioning gives the exact factorial coefficient stated in the proof. For \(n\ge2m\) algebra forces \(a=0\) and \(r=m\), yielding the rectangular expression. Direct bitmask testing of 1,419,214 subsets in 17 instances matches every coefficient; finite testing alone is not treated as the unrestricted proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General graph counting bounds and algorithms do not determine a fixed rook-graph size distribution. Grid graphs built from path/cycle factors are not K_m square K_n for m,n at least three. Published results on different rook-graph vertex properties do not imply dissociation enumeration because the predicates differ; a general-position counting polynomial is not a joint statistic that singles out degree-at-most-one subsets. value.rationale: The theorem enumerates all inclusion-maximal induced-degree-one vertex subsets with their exact size distribution for a natural two-parameter graph family. The coverage/saturation characterization exposes structure that maximum-size theorems omit. For all \(n\ge2m\) it gives a closed single sum, exactly the even cardinalities from \(2\lceil m/2\rceil\) through \(2m\), and an arbitrarily large lower-to-upper maximal-cardinality difference. This is a complete natural classification rather than a scalar exercise or an arbitrary finite slice.
